NEW NAMED CATALYST THIS EDITION - A PHYSICAL SUPPLY LOSS, NOT JUST RISK PREMIUM. Saudi Arabia shut its East-West crude pipeline after drone strikes (attributed in reporting to Iraq-launched and Houthi drones); Reuters and others report the outage threatens roughly 4% of global oil supply if pumping is not resumed within days. This sits on top of the continuing Qatari LNG force majeure and US-Iran hostilities carried through the previous three editions. Unlike 9-10 Sep, there IS a dated catalyst here - name it.

THE CURVE RE-STEEPENED - THIS REVERSES WHAT THE 10 SEP EDITION SAID. On 10 Sep the back of the curve was outrunning the front (Summer/Winter 27 up more than Oct 26) and the note said the term discount was narrowing. Over the weekend that flipped. 10 Sep -> 14 Sep: Oct 26 203.68 -> 207.72 (+2.0%), Winter 26 205.10 -> 211.24 (+3.0%), Dec 26 208.82 -> 213.07 (+2.0%), but Winter 27 129.65 -> 130.25 (+0.5%) and spot 152.00 -> 153.00 (+0.7%). A physical outage prices into the prompt and next winter; the far curve barely moved. Winter 27 now sits 38.3% below Winter 26 (was 36.8%), so THE TERM DISCOUNT HAS WIDENED AGAIN and the 24-month argument is stronger, not weaker. Do not restate the 10 Sep 'discount is narrowing' line - it is superseded.

TWO CONTRACTS HAD NO PRINT ON THIS BOARD AND WERE DROPPED, NOT CARRIED FORWARD: Jan 27 (was 209.45) and Summer 27 (was 136.25) were blank at 09:43. Never re-show a previous edition's price as if it were today's - drop the card.

SUMMER 28 AT 81.60 IS A FIRST APPEARANCE - TREAT WITH MILD CAUTION. It has no history in this file, so unlike Winter 27 (which has held across four editions and is the safe anchor for the term argument) we cannot yet say the level has held. headline: a physical Saudi supply outage has pushed spot up 107% on the year and re-steepened the curve - next winter took the hit, 2027 barely moved
commentary: UK power spot is 153.00 £/MWh, up 107% on a year ago. The market has shifted from geopolitical risk to an actual physical supply loss: Saudi Arabia has shut its East-West crude pipeline after drone strikes, an outage reported to threaten around 4% of global oil supply if pumping does not resume within days, on top of the continuing Qatari LNG force majeure. Day-ahead power followed over the weekend - the N2EX daily average was £168/MWh on 14 September against £127 on 9 September, with the evening peak printing £204.69. What matters for term choice is that the curve has re-steepened. Since Thursday Winter 26 is up 3.0% to 211.24 p/therm while Winter 27 is up just 0.5% to 130.25. A physical outage prices into the prompt and the coming winter; the far curve has barely moved. Winter 27 now sits 38% below Winter 26, a wider gap than a week ago, and Summer 28 is quoted at 81.60. So the case for a longer term has strengthened. A 12-month starting this October buys the most expensive part of the curve outright, while a 24-month blends it with a 2027/28 this shock has largely passed over. The risk premium is concentrated in exactly the months a short contract is most exposed to.

gas.note: NBP front-month (Oct 26) is 207.72 p/therm, with the winter strip higher still - Winter 26 211.24, Dec 26 213.07. The weekend's leg up came from a physical event: Saudi Arabia shutting its East-West crude pipeline after drone strikes, alongside the continuing Qatari LNG force majeure. Note where the move landed - Winter 26 rose 3.0% since Thursday but Winter 27 only 0.5%, at 130.25, and Summer 28 is quoted at 81.60. The shock is concentrated in the coming winter, so the discount further out has widened.
